summary: We created an interactive online 3D application called ‘Gale Traverse’. This application allows users to design walking routes for astronauts to follow on the surface of Gale Crater, Mars. Users can choose any two points on a detailed 3D surface map and the tool will calculate the amount of walking they need to do along the surface, how long it would take to walk there at a realistic speed of 3km/hr (suited astronaut), total climb and elevation difference. Similar to Google Maps. Our project tackles this problem by providing users with a real and scientifically important area (Gale Crater where the Curiosity rover is). This translates planetary data into an engaging visual tool. As opposed to just looking at numbers, users can see the terrain. This is important as we may soon have humans going to Mars, so having well planned traverses is essential. Knowing how far, long and how much elevation change there is means we can make our traverses safer, more efficient and more scientifically informed. We have made this an engaging and intuitive tool for Scientists and the public.
details:
Gale Traverse is an interactive 3D web application that allows users to plan walking routes across Gale Crater on Mars. Users select two points on a detailed 3D terrain model, and the system calculates a path that follows the surface. It then shows the total walking distance, estimated time based on a realistic 3 km/h speed for astronauts in spacesuits, total climb, and height difference. The model can be rotated and zoomed, height information appears when hovering over the surface, and different visual layers can be turned on or off.

The main benefits of the project are that it makes complex Martian terrain easier to understand, allows users to quickly estimate realistic walking distances and times, and clearly shows elevation changes that affect how difficult a route would be. It also gives both the public and researchers a simple way to explore a real NASA landing site.

The intended impact of the project is to support better understanding and planning for future human exploration of Mars. By using real terrain data in an intuitive tool, we aim to help mission planners, students, and space enthusiasts develop a more realistic sense of the challenges of moving across the Martian surface. At the same time, it helps engage a wider audience with planetary science.

The application is web-based and was mainly developed using JavaScript. The 3D terrain is rendered with WebGL. We used a 3D model of Gale Crater in OBJ format along with colour maps and height data. The project was built through an iterative process with the support of AI tools, using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript modules.

What makes the project creative is that it does not simply present static maps or numbers. Instead, it offers an interactive 3D experience similar to Google Earth or Google Maps, but focused on a real location on Mars. Combining actual terrain with practical walking information in one clear interface makes the data more useful and easier to understand.

When developing the project, we focused on usability, scientific relevance, and realism. We chose Gale Crater because of its importance as the landing site of the Curiosity rover. We used a realistic walking speed for astronauts in spacesuits and kept the interface simple so that non-experts could use it easily. We also included elevation and climb information, as these have a major effect on traverse difficulty, while working within the limitations of the available 3D model data, including its approximate scale.

Overall, Gale Traverse is designed to be clear and interactive, so that users can quickly gain useful insights about traversing Martian terrain.
